items.question: A metal toolbox with dimensions 30 cm by 20 cm by 12 cm has a mass of 4.8 kg. The toolbox is initially resting on a workshop floor with its largest face down. A mechanic then flips it to rest on its smallest face. The workshop temperature is 25°C. What is the ratio of the new pressure to the original pressure exerted on the floor?
items.real_world_context: Workshop safety requires understanding how weight distribution affects floor loading and equipment stability
items.explanation: Largest face area = 30 × 20 = 600 cm². Smallest face area = 20 × 12 = 240 cm². The force (weight) remains constant. Original pressure P₁ = F/600. New pressure P₂ = F/240. Ratio P₂:P₁ = (F/240):(F/600) = 600:240 = 5:2. Temperature is irrelevant to the pressure calculation.

items.question: A delivery truck has rectangular tires, each with a contact area of 250 cm² touching the ground. The truck's total mass is 2400 kg, distributed equally across 4 tires. The truck was manufactured in 2018. Calculate the pressure exerted by each tire on the road surface. (Take g = 10 N/kg)
items.real_world_context: Road engineers must calculate tire pressure to design road surfaces that can withstand heavy vehicle loads without damage
items.explanation: Total weight = 2400 kg × 10 N/kg = 24000 N. Weight per tire = 24000 N ÷ 4 = 6000 N. Pressure per tire = 6000 N ÷ 250 cm² = 24 N/cm². The manufacturing year is irrelevant information.

items.question: A brick with dimensions 25 cm by 15 cm by 8 cm has a mass of 3 kg. It is placed on soft ground with its largest face down. A builder then repositions it to rest on its smallest face. The brick's color is red. What is the ratio of the final pressure to the initial pressure on the ground?
items.real_world_context: Construction workers must understand pressure distribution to prevent bricks from sinking into soft ground during building
items.explanation: Largest face area = 25 × 15 = 375 cm². Smallest face area = 15 × 8 = 120 cm². Force remains constant. Initial pressure P₁ = F/375. Final pressure P₂ = F/120. Ratio P₂:P₁ = (F/120):(F/375) = 375:120 = 25:8. The brick's color is irrelevant.

items.question: A rectangular storage container with base dimensions 80 cm by 50 cm is filled with cooking oil to a height of 60 cm. The density of the oil is 0.9 g/cm³. The container was purchased for $45. Calculate the pressure exerted by the oil on the base of the container. (Take g = 10 N/kg)
items.real_world_context: Food industry storage facilities must calculate liquid pressure to ensure containers can safely hold large volumes of oil without rupturing
items.explanation: Volume of oil = 80 × 50 × 60 = 240000 cm³. Mass = 240000 cm³ × 0.9 g/cm³ = 216000 g = 216 kg. Weight = 216 kg × 10 N/kg = 2160 N. Base area = 80 × 50 = 4000 cm². Pressure = 2160 N ÷ 4000 cm² = 0.54 N/cm². The purchase price is irrelevant

If the block is then turned to rest on its smallest face instead, by how many times does the pressure on the table increase? (Take 1 kg = 10 N)
concept_tags: inverse relationship between pressure and area
items.real_world_context: Understanding how pressure changes when objects are oriented differently is important in construction, furniture design, and preventing floor damage from heavy objects.

items.question: A water tank has a rectangular base measuring 80 cm by 50 cm. Water is poured into the tank at a rate of 4 litres per minute. The tank was initially empty and has a height of 60 cm. What is the pressure exerted by the water on the base of the tank after 5 minutes of filling? (Take 1 litre = 1000 cm³ and pressure from water = height in cm × 0.1 N/cm²)
items.real_world_context: Water pressure calculations are essential for designing water storage systems, aquariums, and ensuring structural integrity of tanks and dams.
items.explanation: Volume of water added = 4 litres/min × 5 min = 20 litres = 20 × 1000 cm³ = 20,000 cm³. Base area = 80 cm × 50 cm = 4000 cm

items.question: A rectangular wooden block with dimensions 20 cm by 15 cm by 10 cm has a mass of 1.8 kg. The block is painted blue on all sides. When the block is placed on a table with its largest face in contact with the surface, what pressure does it exert on the table? (Take 1 kg of mass to exert a force of 10 N)
items.real_world_context: Furniture placement and floor loading in homes
items.explanation: First, convert mass to force: 1.8 kg × 10 N/kg = 18 N. The largest face has dimensions 20 cm × 15 cm = 300 cm². Convert to m²: 300 cm² = 0.03 m². Pressure = Force ÷ Area = 18 N ÷ 0.03 m² = 600 Pa. The irrelevant datum is the blue paint. Option A (60 Pa) is a trap for students who use 0.3 m² instead of 0.03 m². Option C (120 Pa) traps students who calculate area incorrectly as 20 × 15 = 300 and divide 18 ÷ 300 without proper unit conversion. Option D (1200 Pa) traps students who use the smallest face area.

items.question: A water tank has a square base with sides of 80 cm. Water is poured into the tank at a rate of 12 litres per minute for 5 minutes. The tank was initially empty and has a total height of 150 cm. What is the pressure exerted by the water on the base of the tank at the end of the 5 minutes? (Take the density of water as 1000 kg/m³ and 1 kg of mass to exert a force of 10 N. Note: 1 litre = 1000 cm³)
items.real_world_context: Water storage systems and tank design
items.explanation: Total volume poured = 12 litres/min × 5 min = 60 litres = 60,000 cm³. Base area = 80 cm × 80 cm = 6400 cm². Height of water = 60,000 cm³ ÷ 6400 cm² = 9.375 cm = 0.09375 m. Pressure = density × g × height = 1000 kg/m³ × 10 N/kg × 0.09375 m = 937.5 Pa. The irrelevant datum is the total tank height (150 cm). Option B (9375 Pa) traps students who use 9.375 cm without converting to metres. Option C (750 Pa) traps students who calculate 60,000 ÷ 80 = 750. Option D (7500 Pa) combines errors from options B and C.

items.question: A metal cube with edge length 5 cm and mass 600 g is placed on a soft foam surface. The cube is then replaced by a metal cylinder of the same mass with a circular base of radius 2 cm and height 8 cm. What is the ratio of the pressure exerted by the cube to the pressure exerted by the cylinder on the foam surface?
items.real_world_context: Material deformation and surface damage prevention
items.explanation: Since both objects have the same mass, they exert the same force. Pressure ratio = (Force/Area_cube) : (Force/Area_cylinder) = Area_cylinder : Area_cube. Cube base area = 5 cm × 5 cm = 25 cm². Cylinder base area = π × 2² = 4π ≈ 12.56 cm². Ratio = 25 : 12.56. Using π ≈ 3.14, we get 25 : 12.56 ≈ 25 : 12.5 = 50 : 25 = 2 : 1. items.question: A rectangular wooden block has dimensions 20 cm by 15 cm by 10 cm and a mass of 1.8 kg. The block is placed on a horizontal table. Initially, it rests on its largest face. Sarah then repositions the block so that it rests on its smallest face instead. The table has a total surface area of 5000 cm². What is the ratio of the pressure exerted on the table in the new position to the pressure in the initial position?
concept_tags: inverse relationship between pressure and area
items.real_world_context: Placing objects on different faces to distribute weight differently on surfaces, such as furniture placement to avoid floor damage
items.explanation: The force (weight) remains constant at 1.8 kg regardless of orientation. The table's total surface area (5000 cm²) is irrelevant information. Initial position: largest face = 20 cm × 15 cm = 300 cm². New position: smallest face = 15 cm × 10 cm = 150 cm². Since Pressure = Force ÷ Area, and force is constant, pressure is inversely proportional to area. Ratio of new pressure to initial pressure = (Initial Area) ÷ (New Area) = 300 ÷ 150 = 2 ÷ 1 = 2 : 1. Option B (3:2) is a trap for students who might incorrectly calculate the ratio using the dimensions 20:15 or 15:10. Option C (2:3) traps students who invert the ratio. Option D (1:2) traps students who calculate initial to new instead of new to initial.
